source: Hypercar cooling system (car_hyper, car_hyper_n2o), sized from the heat load of its 5.1 L twin-turbo V8 (data/engine_thermal/hyper_v8_one1.json). The class passenger-car radiator (0.35 m2, UA 1500 W/K at 2.0 kg/s air) cannot carry it: at full power the engine puts about 3.06 MW of released fuel energy into the cylinders (measured on the final car by the diag in tests/unit/test_game_car_thermal.cpp at 427 km/h, 7636 rpm: 612 kW wall heat = wall_heat_fraction 0.20 [AS, class, pinned to the turbo configuration's 0.20] x 3.06 MW, plus 88 kW friction heat of which 30 % goes to the oil), against a design target in the brief of 2.5 MW fuel and 400-500 kW to the coolant; the class radiator with its own 0.35 ram coefficient reaches only about 4.6 kW/K at 427 km/h and would need 612/4.6 = 133 K above ambient, so the coolant passes the 118 C overheat warning within seconds of a full-throttle pull. Sizing [D]/[AS]: the class core is scaled by frontal area, which keeps its construction and its UA-per-area at equal face velocity: A = 1.0 m2 [AS: three radiators, e.g. two front cores and one in the tail, of about 0.33 m2 each; real cars of this class use several], UA_ref = 1500 W/K x (1.0/0.35) = 4286 W/K at air_mass_flow_ref = 2.0 kg/s x (1.0/0.35) = 5.714 kg/s (the same 4.8 m/s face velocity as the class core), exponent 0.6 as the class [C, Incropera & DeWitt]. ram_coefficient 0.20 [AS]: face velocity = 0.20 x airspeed, ducted cores behind an inlet (the class 0.35 is an open sedan grille; at 427 km/h 0.35 would be an unphysical 41 m/s through the core). Fan [AS]: 6.0 m/s face velocity (twin electric fans on the larger area, the class value is 3.5); on/off 98/93 C, warnings 118/50 C and the needle curve are the class values. oil_cooler.air_w_k_per_m_s 0.6 [AS]: an air-oil cooler of about 0.6 W/K per m/s of airspeed (about 70 W/K at 427 km/h on top of the engine file's 1.27 W/K per m/s block-oil term); without it the oil lump rose past 125 C and was still rising after 90 s at top speed (oil-air only 160 W/K for 26 kW of oil heat); with it the oil ends the 90 s hold at 111 C. Design target: the coolant stays below the 118 C overheat threshold for at least 60 s of sustained full throttle at top speed with ram air, and in the normal band (below the fan's 98 C) at a steady 130 km/h. Measured with the final files (flat 40 km strip, assist auto-shift, ISA 15 C, warm start 91 C): full throttle from standstill peaks at 105.2 C during the pull (350 km/h at about t = 20 s, thermostat opening, fan on), then settles at 99.1 C on the 427 km/h plateau with the thermostat fully open and the radiator at its limit (7.6 kW/K, 635 kW), oil 111 C after 90 s at top speed and still creeping up; on a 35 C day the same run peaks at 117 C, just under the warning, and a very long full-throttle run on a hotter day overheats, which is realistic. 130 km/h cruise: coolant 85-92 C regulated by the thermostat (93 C on a 35 C day), never above the fan threshold. The nitrous hypercar shares this file and is not tuned for the shot: with the kit armed the full-throttle pull peaks at 119.4 C at ISA (about 5 s above the 118 C warning, from 22 s, then back to 100 C once the 35 s shot ends) and 132.6 C on a 35 C day, because the shot raises the released fuel energy to about 4.7 MW (940 kW wall heat).
